title: Adding transaction savepoints interpolated the caller-supplied savepoint name into SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE statements with f-strings.

findings.explanation: The code constructs SQL with a savepoint name, but now validates the name using `validate_savepoint_name()` which enforces a strict allowlist of characters (letters, digits, dash, underscore). This prevents SQL injection by rejecting any input containing SQL metacharacters. The validation occurs before the SQL is constructed.

evidence.content:
async def rollback_to(self):
        validate_savepoint_name(self.name)
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

findings.explanation: Same mitigation as postgres.py: savepoint names are validated with `validate_savepoint_name()` before use in SQL queries, enforcing a strict allowlist that prevents SQL injection.
